request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (50,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 36.1% (95% band 34.2% to 38.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.246: -0.72; 0.246 <= x < 0.414: -0.297445; 0.414 <= x < 0.584: -0.01; 0.584 <= x < 0.618: +0.39; 0.618 <= x < 0.668: +0.81; 0.668 <= x < 0.729: +1.52; 0.729 <= x < 0.782: +2.3; 0.782 <= x < 0.875: +3.36; x >= 0.875: +4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.90, 95% band [+2.76, +3.23]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 21.1% (95% band 18.5% to 22.1%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.2; >= 2: +0.6 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.93, 95% band [+0.82, +1.00]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 12.1% (95% band 11.0% to 14.0%); rank 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 28,600: +0.4; 28,600 <= x < 49,700: +0.12; 49,700 <= x < 95,200: -0.14; x >= 95,200: -0.5 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.96, 95% band [-1.12, -0.83]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 8.6% (95% band 7.2% to 9.8%); rank 4 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 66.3: +0.296; 66.3 <= x < 253: -0.01; x >= 253: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.67, 95% band [-0.77, -0.54]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 6.7% (95% band 5.3% to 7.9%); rank 4 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.444: -0.07; x >= 0.444: +0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.29, 95% band [+0.21, +0.39]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 3.3% (95% band 2.5% to 4.2%); rank 6 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2: -0.04; 3-4: +0.13; >= 5: +0.4 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.35, 95% band [+0.21, +0.44]).
- `feature_b`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.5% to 3.1%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.05, 95% band [-0.14, +0.03]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 1.7% (95% band 0.5% to 3.1%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.04, 95% band [-0.16, +0.03]).
- `feature_a`: an application attribute (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.6% to 3.3%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.06, 95% band [-0.01, +0.15]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `history_months & n_inquiries`: share of importance 3.8% (95% band 2.3% to 4.6%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 23.6 to 342: -0.32 (95% band -0.50 to -0.17) when `n_inquiries` = 0, -1.29 (95% band -1.47 to -1.02) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.84 (95% band +0.60 to +0.98) when `history_months` = 23.6, -0.13 (95% band -0.30 to +0.09) when `history_months` = 342.
- `age & feature_b`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `age` from 23.8 to 72.3: +0.19 (95% band -0.13 to +0.26) when `feature_b` = -1.64, -0.23 (95% band -0.38 to +0.02) when `feature_b` = 1.64.
  Effect of `feature_b` from -1.64 to 1.64: +0.13 (95% band -0.13 to +0.22) when `age` = 23.8, -0.29 (95% band -0.39 to +0.02) when `age` = 72.3.
- `utilization & feature_a`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.5%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0965 to 0.749: +2.88 (95% band +2.73 to +3.23) when `feature_a` = -1.66, +3.06 (95% band +2.76 to +3.37) when `feature_a` = 1.65.
  Effect of `feature_a` from -1.66 to 1.65: -0.07 (95% band -0.19 to +0.15) when `utilization` = 0.0965, +0.11 (95% band -0.01 to +0.24) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0965 to 0.749: +2.85 (95% band +2.76 to +3.17) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +2.97 (95% band +2.76 to +3.27) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: +0.91 (95% band +0.80 to +0.99) when `utilization` = 0.0965, +1.04 (95% band +0.82 to +1.14) when `utilization` = 0.749.
- 1 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 0.4%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"Revolving credit utilization is the strongest driver of default predictions, accounting for about 36% of the model's importance, and its effect is steep: applicants using most of their credit limit (roughly 0.875 and above) add about 4 units to the log-odds of default, while those using less than about 0.25 of their limit reduce it by about 0.72."},{"id":2,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver (about 21%): having no delinquencies lowers predicted risk, one delinquency raises it slightly, and two or more raise it further."},{"id":3,"text":"Income is third (about 12%), with lower incomes raising predicted default risk and incomes above about $95,200 lowering it."},{"id":4,"text":"Length of credit history and the debt-to-income ratio each matter less (about 9% and 7%): shorter histories (under about 66 months) and debt-to-income ratios of 0.444 or more push risk up, while longer histories lower it."},{"id":5,"text":"Recent credit inquiries have a smaller effect (about 3%), raising predicted risk only when there are five or more."},{"id":6,"text":"The interaction between credit history and recent inquiries is worth noting: a short history combined with many inquiries pushes predicted risk up more than either factor alone, whereas for applicants with long histories the number of inquiries makes little difference."},{"id":7,"text":"Age, feature_a and feature_b contribute very little, and the data do not settle whether they affect predictions in any consistent direction."}]}
